rv.q: The Blue Violinist Over West End Avenue is a great and thoughtful show that delivers quite a bit of bang for the buck.
Whatever your own views, you can see it’s not a fair fight.
This show revitalizes the validity of Jewish perspectives with nuance, understanding, and clarity in a beautiful way that invites people in and doesn’t ask for permission.
But as a play, The Blue Violinist Over West End Avenue is a Shabbat dinner you may want to skip.
The Blue Violinist Over West End Avenue begins with a celebration and becomes a reckoning: with the price of acceptance, the obligations of memory, and the limits of loyalty.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this family drama exploring Jewish identity and October 7th. While some praise its historical context and emotional resonance, others find it dramatically inert, with characters reduced to debating positions.
